meta.title: Async handler — the worker handles other work while suspended
meta.subtitle: while H1 gives up the thread on await, the worker runs H2 first, and H1 resumes when the response arrives

messages.label: worker moves to the next work — run HandleAsync()

cards.title: Non-blocking interleaving
items: When H1 suspends at the await Request point, only that flow of execution pauses and the thread returns to the pool — it holds no thread.
The worker immediately picks up the next work (H2) and runs it, and H2 finishes before H1's response arrives.

cards.title: resume
items: When the Play channel's response arrives, H1 resumes on the spot and returns.

So a handful of workers handle huge numbers of concurrent requests with code that reads top to bottom, no callbacks. Blocking with .Result keeps the thread occupied, so it's forbidden inside a handler.
